title: Handling Varied Objectives by Online Decision Making

problem.claim: Learning systems commonly assume a fixed objective, but real-world tasks may require optimization of dynamically changing objective weights.

gap.claim: Existing fixed-objective learning formulations do not address sequential decision making under varied objectives in open and dynamic environments.

contributions.claim: The VaRons algorithm estimates action-wise performance on multiple sub-objectives and adaptively selects actions according to dynamic requirements.
The Con-VaRons algorithm extends the approach to contextual representations under a parameterized linear structure linking contextual features to the main objective.
The paper establishes minimax optimality with respect to the time horizon for both VaRons and Con-VaRons, with Con-VaRons having better dependency on the number of sub-objectives.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on dynamic classifier and real-world cluster service allocation tasks validate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.
The experiments support the theoretical findings.

narrative_sequence.summary: Fixed learning objectives are inadequate when real-world objectives change over time.
The paper formulates learning with varied objectives and introduces VaRons, then extends it to contextual settings with Con-VaRons.
Both methods are described as minimax optimal, and experiments are reported on dynamic classification and cluster service allocation.

source_observation.claim: The method models changing priorities as a dynamic weighted combination of multiple sub-objectives.

interpretation.claim: Separating sub-objective performance can support adaptive decisions when the relative importance of goals changes.

application.claim: This approach may apply to sequential systems whose priorities vary with context or user needs.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish applicability beyond the stated objective model and contextual linear structure.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact minimax guarantees.
The abstract does not provide experimental datasets, baselines, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not detail the dynamic objective-weighting process.
